topology: PC1 and PC2 share a prepared access switch and R1 client LAN. R1 has separate routed SRV1 HTTP and SRV2 DNS/HTTP LANs. All addresses, gateways, services and VLAN1 switching are prepared.
implemented: Fourth ENCOR Security lab and36 total ENCOR entries; original CCNA standard, extended and named/numbered ACL labs remain available. Share links retain the current host/path/query.

An unfiltered four-path baseline precedes a named source-only standard ACL. CLIENT-SOURCES permits the PC1 host before denying the broader client subnet, applied outbound only toward SRV1. Three ACL-permitted PC1 replies, PC2 drops and fresh unaffected PC2/SRV2 replies prove the destination scope.

Migration retains the standard list but removes its binding. EDGE-POLICY alone filters R1 Gi0/0 inbound with ordered destination TCP80, UDP53 and ICMP echo permits followed by the explicit SRV1 IP deny.

Actual full HTTP responses, receiver-confirmed fresh DNS answers, three correlated ACL-permitted echo replies and explicit/implicit packet drops distinguish protocols and destinations. A TCP80 permit cannot satisfy ICMP, and DNS permission cannot satisfy the DNS server HTTP service.

Controlled first-match shadowing, incorrect HTTP destination/source port, incorrect DNS protocol/port and reversed interface direction produce real drops. Repair requires new correctly filtered traffic after the observed fault; earlier successes cannot substitute.
The reversed-direction incident requires an actual server-accepted echo request and its reply dropped on R1 client egress, followed by three fresh permitted replies after restoring inbound placement.
Temporarily unbinding an intact list permits an actual complete PC2 web page without applied ACL decisions. Final live binding and save requirements force restoration.

Both IOS clear access-list counters aliases retain their operational behavior. A bounded32-entry runtime reset history records target name, time and pre-clear counts. The lesson requires populated named counts, prior packet decisions and fresh successful/denied HTTP after clearing; empty, unrelated or global clears cannot substitute. Other ACL counters remain separate.

The final saved state requires exact restored lists, exclusive operational inbound placement, R1 startup equality, active routing and prepared addresses/gateways, VLAN1 switch access paths, enabled server services/DNS record, five healthy links and no other node ACL bindings.

Practice starts0/20; completed reference supplies four live configuration/save tasks with empty runtime and no invented traffic, repair or reset achievements. Earned observations survive YAML while counters, reset history and packet state clear on reopen.

New criteria use bounded enums and fixed teaching roots; missing required interfaces and foreign roots fail closed. Counter edits, cached DNS and advisory ACL checks alone do not create packet observations.
scope: Working IOS IPv4 standard and extended interface ACLs, host/wildcard matching, first-match sequence editing, ingress/egress behavior and named counters. Filtering decisions and packet forwarding are unchanged.
ACL resequence automation, ACL log/syslog aggregation, fragmentation matches, scheduled ACLs and stateful firewall behavior are not configured or claimed by this lab.
Primary Cisco ACL documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed; existing IOS/NX-OS CML contracts are covered by full regression.
No UI theme/layout, terminal styling, node artwork, dependency or backend/server changes.
